subject: SIG: Hosting ownership & controls — concise brief for CISO review
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@stellarishealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-08-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG follow-up — need clear hosting ownership summary

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the SIG packet earlier. Our audit team has one outstanding ask: a one-page plain-English summary that maps each SIG control area (networking, key management, logging/audit, data residency) to who controls and operates it under each Redwood deployment mode — Hosted, Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Private (VPC/on-prem). They want something short we can attach to our audit folder rather than re-reading the full SIG spreadsheet.

Key constraints:
- Emphasize what Stellaris must configure/own vs what Redwood manages.
- Call out where additional contractual options (KMS integration, retained logs export, SOC 2 attestations) are required.
- Any differences in telemetry retention and access patterns across modes.

Can you provide that? We're aiming to close our SIG review by next Wednesday.

Best,
Alyssa Chen
CISO Office — Stellaris Health

Attachment: existing SIG export (we sent earlier)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@stellarishealth.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-08-19T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — need clear hosting ownership summary

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clear ask.

I'll keep this concise and practical. Drafting a one-page ownership map and attaching the working matrix. Looping in Vivek for technical accuracy and Aditya for contractual options (KMS / audit exports). Monica from the compliance team will give a final read for wording we can attach to your audit file.

Deliverables we will provide by COB Monday:
- One-page ownership summary (PDF) that maps responsibilities across Hosted / Dedicated / Private.
- Highlighted SIG controls that change ownership or require add-ons.
- A short appendix with links to SOC 2 report location and how to request KMS integrations.

Quick note on scope so we align: for "Hosted" we will call out that TLS termination and model runtime are Redwood-managed and multi-tenant logical isolation applies; for "Dedicated" the compute is committed and log access/segregation is stronger with per-tenant pools; for "Private/VPC/on-prem" your team or infra partner runs the control plane and can enforce customer-managed keys and network egress controls. We'll be explicit about default telemetry retention and options to export or change retention via a support request.

Will share the draft shortly.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@stellarishealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-08-20T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — need clear hosting ownership summary

Alyssa / team — attaching a technical sketch and the ownership matrix we discussed. Below are the operational callouts I suggested be in the one-pager (short, actionable bullets):

Hosted (Redwood API):
- Responsibilities: Redwood manages model runtime, TLS termination at our edge, host-level patching, and multi-tenant logical isolation.
- Customer responsibilities: Prompt/content, API keys, integration-side logging, and opt-in telemetry export.
- Security controls: SOC 2 in place; standard logging retention 90 days (configurable via support contract).
- KMS/keys: Bring-your-own-key (BYOK) not available by default; customer-managed key support is offered on Dedicated/Private with contractual integration.

Dedicated (Reserved Capacity):
- Responsibilities: Redwood provides per-customer GPU pools, network segmentation, and stronger tenant isolation; we manage the infrastructure but provide segregated logging streams.
- Customer responsibilities: API keys, workload-level RBAC, and any client-side encryption.
- Security controls: Option to enable KMS with per-tenant CMKs; extended log retention and filtered export available as an add-on.

Private (VPC / On‑prem):
- Responsibilities: Customer operates private control plane (or we install a private instance), controls network egress, and can configure HSM/KMS for key custody. Redwood provides deployment automation and support but operational control sits with the customer.
- Customer responsibilities: Network configuration, host OS management (if on-prem), access control, and KMS/HSM provisioning.
- Security controls: Full audit log access, customizable retention, and local data residency.

Audit-specific notes:
- Audit logs: For Hosted and Dedicated, Redwood can export logs (S3/GCS) to a customer-owned bucket on request; Private deployments can keep logs entirely on-customer infrastructure.
- Data residency: Hosted regions are specified at signup; Dedicated offers region pinning; Private supports on-prem residency.
- Evidence: SOC 2 reports available via our compliance portal; SIG responses and L2 evidence (architecture diagrams, runbooks) can be shared under NDA.

Attaching: hosting-ownership-matrix.pdf (one-page brief), SIG-answers-v1.xlsx (working answers), kms-diagram.png

—Vivek
VP, Platform Security, Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@stellarishealth.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-08-22T14:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — need clear hosting ownership summary

Alyssa — attaching the final one-page PDF for your audit folder (hosting-ownership-matrix.pdf). Key changes since the draft: we added explicit line items for network egress controls, clarified default telemetry retention windows, and listed the support path to request KMS integration or SOC 2 evidence.

TL;DR (pasteable into your audit notes):
- Hosted: Redwood-managed runtime; standard telemetry retention 90 days; SOC 2 available; BYOK/KMS requires upgrade to Dedicated or Private.
- Dedicated: Customer-dedicated GPU pools with stronger isolation; optional KMS integration and extended log export as add-ons; contractual SLA available.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Customer-managed infrastructure and keys; full control over retention & egress; Redwood provides deployment automation and support under enterprise license.

Next steps if you want us to tailor wording for a specific SIG control id: tell us which control(s) (e.g., CC6.1, EN3.2) and we’ll produce a 1–2 sentence mapping per control for your folder.

Thanks — happy to join a quick call if the audit team prefers a walkthrough.

Best,
Lauren
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: hosting-ownership-matrix.pdf, SIG-answers-v1.xlsx, kms-diagram.png
